subject: PostgreSQL 19 Released 🐘, Booking.com’s AI Rebuild 🏗️, Claude Starts Most Agent Pipelines 🤖
notes: No funding rounds, acquisitions, IPOs, funds or model pricing in this issue. Only product/engineering items; the main ones are listed as other/product.

stories.headline: PostgreSQL 19 released
stories.quote: PostgreSQL 19 lets teams reclaim disk space without blocking reads or writes and gives them more control over query plans.

stories.headline: Grafana introduces Grafana Notebooks
stories.quote: Grafana Notebooks bring charts, queries, and findings from Grafana Assistant into one shareable working document.
stories.description: Shareable working documents for charts, queries and findings

stories.headline: OpenMetadata 2.1 adds semantic context features to the open-source catalog
stories.quote: OpenMetadata 2.1 turns the open-source catalog into more of a semantic context layer: it imports metric definitions from warehouses and BI tools, adds hierarchies and finer-grained lineage, and exposes an RDF knowledge graph through MCP.

stories.headline: Microsoft presents database updates at Ignite 2026
stories.quote: Microsoft is folding transactional databases, governance, vector search, and Fabric into one AI-ready stack, tightening integration across the database estate.

stories.headline: dltHub reports Claude Code started 92% of agent-run dlt pipelines in October
stories.quote: AI coding agents can now build, run, and fix dlt data pipelines with little human input, and Claude Code started 92% of agent-run pipelines in October.

facts.text: About 28,000 distinct custom data sources in use, versus roughly 700 connectors in a typical catalog
facts.quote: dltHub tracked about 28,000 distinct custom data sources in use, compared with roughly 700 connectors in a typical catalog.
